decisions.reason: Although more niche and commercially uncertain than the chamber products, the particle-therapy water phantom is still closely tied to the firm's dosimetry and QA knowledge base, giving it a reasonable chance of improvement and retention.

A small-volume ionization chamber builds directly on the firm's core calibration, measurement, and radiation-therapy QA capabilities, so management would usually continue it unless early field performance were clearly poor.
This product is highly related to existing technical and service competences, and any early market feedback can likely be absorbed and used to refine rather than abandon it.
A standard clinical ionization chamber line sits at the center of the firm's established expertise and customer base, making discontinuation within a year unlikely.

An ionization chamber for relative dosimetry strongly matches the firm's accumulated know-how, accredited calibration resources, and clinical workflow offering, so it is more likely to be maintained than dropped.
The thimble ionization chamber is a classic adjacent product for this firm's radiation-measurement portfolio, and its strong knowledge fit supports continued commercialization.
